releases.body:
0.5.11 waited 1200 ms, then 2400 ms, and gave up. That is the right shape for a host with nothing behind a 429 — the bucket is spent and a longer wait only postpones the same answer.

But this package is distributed, and some deployments do have something behind a 429: when the egress rotates, the same request answers once the exit has changed, and a retry that gives up in 3.6 s can never reach that point.

- `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MAX_MS` is new: it raises the ceiling the doubling stops at (default still `5000`, ceiling `120000`).
- It is floored at the first wait (`OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MS`), so the two cannot be set to contradict each other and the backoff can never shrink.
- **Every default is unchanged.** A host that sets nothing gets exactly what 0.5.11 gave it: 2 retries, 1200 ms, ceiling 5000 ms.
- A deployment that rotates can ask for 5000 → 10000 → 20000 ms and land after the change.
- Out-of-range values fall back to the default rather than reaching the timer.

Measured on a deployment with a rotating egress: a fresh (exit, project id) pair answered 200 in 6 of 6 rotations, while changing only one of the two answered 429 — so the wait has to reach past the rotation for a retry to be worth spending.

node --test 823 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

0.5.10 retried a 429, but only a 429: a `fetch` that throws produces no `Response`, so the retry never saw it and the exception went straight to the host, which reports it as a quota failure.

Measured 2026-10-27 on a live deployment: an egress mid-switch pointed the proxy at `127.0.0.1:1`, the request never left the machine (`dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connection refused`, and zero connections to `opencode.ai` in that window), and DeepSeek Harness was told `429 … QUOTA`. The path came back four seconds later and the same request answered 200 — a turn lost to a failure this package could see and did not retry.

- A request that never got an answer is now retried alongside a 429. The loop spends its waits and then hands the failure on as itself, rather than inventing a Response.
- `looksLikeTransportFailure` recognises the connection-shaped errors: `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENETUNREACH`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `ENETDOWN`, `EPIPE`, the undici codes, and the `proxyconnect` wording.
- A caller's own abort is never retried: it is the one thing the caller said about this request.
- A failure that cannot confidently be called transient is not retried either, so a real fault still surfaces as itself rather than as three identical failures.
- Verified on the deployment: the refused connection now takes 3621 ms to surface, which is the two default waits (1200 + 2400) being spent; before this change it failed instantly.
- node --test 822 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

The free quota is ledged per project id and egress together, so a spent bucket is not a spent exit. A host does not recover from a 429 on its own — DeepSeek Harness ends the turn and reports the quota as exhausted — so a request the route would have served under a new ledger used to be a dead turn.

- A 429 is now retried with a project id and a session id nothing has spent, and the same bytes are sent again. The retry's answer is the turn.
- Only a 429 is retried: a 403 is the fingerprint or the egress, a 426 the version, a 5xx the endpoint failing, and none of those is answered differently under a new id.
- A 429 whose body names abuse of the egress is not retried — an id is not an IP.
- A project id the host named itself (`x-opencode-project`, or a git project magpie hands over) is kept on every attempt: that name is the host's statement about itself.
- Off with `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_429=0` (2 retries by default). The wait comes from `OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_RETRY_WAIT_MS` (1200ms, doubling, clamped 100–5000). Both are read per request.
- The refusal that finally leaves is the route's own, untouched, so a genuinely exhausted account still reads as one.
- `.gitattributes` states the line endings once, so a CRLF checkout is no longer a 40k-line diff.
- node --test 820 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

The free quota is ledged per project id and egress together — measured 2026-10-26: from an exit answering 429 to the genuine CLI under one project id, the same CLI under a brand-new project id answered 200, and a random 40-hex id in this package's own shape answered 200 from a spent exit, twice. The old default `global` is the project id every freeriding plugin user's traffic carries, so its buckets on popular exits arrive pre-burned — which is how a freshly rotated exit once answered 429 twenty-one seconds after first use.

- A request whose host names a project — by `x-opencode-project` or with a git project magpie hands over — keeps that name. A request whose host does not gets a git-hash-shaped id of its own per request (`randomProjectID`): a ledger no other traffic shares, wherever the request lands.
- The gate probes the same way: `tools-smoke.mjs` asks with a fresh project id per probe, or it would report a wording refusal where the truth is a spent `global` bucket.
- Both READMEs and MAINTAINING.md state the pair-keyed ledger and the sharing trap, with the measurements.
- node --test 799 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).

The 2.1.4 prompt commands the model to use `execute`, and the official set rides in the tools array because the gates read it — so a model that believes its prompt opened the session by calling `execute` to an unknown-tool error, then the catalog's `shell` to another, before finding the `clint_` names on the third call (measured 2026-10-25 on DeepSeek Harness, twice per session).

- The official prompt is now followed by a `<system-reminder>` — the prompt's own convention for harness instruction — stating that Code Mode is not active here, that the built-ins are not implemented, and naming the `clint_` tools this host actually runs, enumerated per request from the renaming's own output. A host that declared no tools is told so outright.
- The tier does not check the prompt byte for byte — the skills listing was removed in 0.5.5 and the whole 2.1.4 text swapped in 0.5.7, both answered — and this one was verified live too: the full shaping path with the note answered 200 from a live exit under Bun.
- Tests pin the note: names enumerated from the body's `clint_` entries, the no-tools branch, the note sitting between the official prompt and the host's own instructions, and an already-shaped body left untouched.
- node --test 799 pass (the 8 capture tests want Bun).
